abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    In this work, we present a comprehensive technology computer-aided design investigation of charge trap layer engineering and channel material effects in three-dimensional (3D) vertical NAND flash memory cells. Using Silvaco Atlas with the DYNASONOS charge trapping model, we systematically analyze the impact of trap density (
                    <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>T</jats:sub>
                    ), tunneling oxide (
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>OX</jats:sub>
                    ) thickness, and polysilicon channel properties on program/erase (P/E) characteristics, memory window, and device reliability. Our simulation results reveal that the optimal trap density for maximizing the P/E window is approximately 3–5 × 10
                    <jats:sup>19</jats:sup>
                    cm
                    <jats:sup>−3</jats:sup>
                    , beyond which the incremental window gain saturates. A tunnel oxide thickness of 4–5 nm provides the best trade-off between programming speed and long-term data retention, demonstrating ⩽15% charge loss over 10 years when combined with an optimized Al
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    blocking oxide. Furthermore, we investigate the effect of polysilicon grain boundary traps on threshold voltage (
                    <jats:italic>V</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>th</jats:sub>
                    ) variability, showing that larger grain sizes (>50 nm) significantly reduce the
                    <jats:italic>V</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>th</jats:sub>
                    distribution width. The simulation methodology is calibrated validated against published experimental P/E, retention, and endurance data, and coupled parameter optimization guidelines are provided for next-generation high-density 3D NAND flash memory design.
                  </jats:p>
title: TCAD-based investigation of charge trap layer engineering and channel effects on program/erase characteristics in 3D vertical NAND flash memory cells
